title: Criminal Reference on City Harvest Church Matter
what_it_is: Criminal Reference on City Harvest Church Matter

sections.label: Court of Appeal Reference decision
sections.summary: On 1 February 2018 the Court of Appeal released its decision on the Reference.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: On 1 February 2018, last week, the Court of Appeal released its decision on the Reference.

sections.label: Officers liable under Penal Code section 406
sections.summary: The Court of Appeal ruled officers are liable under section 406 of the Penal Code, punishable by up to seven years' imprisonment, or fine, or both, and are not professional agents liable under section 409.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The Court of Appeal ruled that such officers are liable to be punished under section 406 of the Penal Code that provides for a maximum sentence of seven years’ imprisonment, or fine, or both.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The Court of Appeal also ruled that these officers do not come within the term, the meaning of a professional “agent”, and therefore, they were not liable for the more serious penalties under section 409 of the Penal Code for CBT.

sections.label: Lacuna in the law
sections.summary: The Court of Appeal's decision means there is now a lacuna in the law.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The Court of Appeal's decision means that there is now a lacuna in the law.

sections.label: Parliament to amend law
sections.summary: It is up to Parliament to amend the law soon, and legislation will provide higher penalties for directors and other senior officers who commit CBT.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: It is now up to Parliament to amend the law, and that we should do soon.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: We will ensure that legislation provides for higher penalties for directors and other senior officers who commit CBT.

sections.label: Prosecuting people who abuse judges
sections.summary: People who abuse judges and challenge their integrity will be prosecuted if a case for contempt can be made out.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: People who abuse judges, challenge their integrity will be prosecuted if a case for contempt can be made out.

sections.label: Administration of Justice (Protection) Act
sections.summary: If left alone they will become the norm, which is why the Administration of Justice (Protection) Act was legislated into law.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: If left alone, they will become the norm.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: That is why we legislated into law the Administration of Justice (Protection) Act.

sections.label: Faked headline in Facebook post
sections.summary: A Facebook post faked a newspaper headline about a PAP lawyer, which the AGC views as contempt by scandalising the Courts.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The title of the news article, the banner headlines had, however, been faked in the Facebook post.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Someone appeared to have faked the title into, and I quote, "PAP lawyer saved the accused from harsher penalties", making it look as if a mass circulation newspaper had done so, probably to give more credence to the headline.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: AGC's view is that this is a case of contempt by scandalising the Courts.

sections.label: IHT instructing counsel decision
sections.summary: The IHT's decision to instruct the speaker was called the highest tribute to counsel's integrity and possibly reflected on the Government's integrity.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The decision by the IHT, despite the situation, to instruct me was, and I quote "the highest tribute to the integrity of the counsel" and "possibly reflected also on the integrity of the Government".

sections.label: Fake headlines and mob mentality
sections.summary: The fake headline reflects a mob mentality to intimidate lawyers, and accepting such faking risks mainstream media abusing judges as in the UK.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The fake headline that I referred to earlier in the Facebook page is part of a mob mentality, to hound the lawyers, to intimidate them into not acting in cases which the mob disapproves of.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Supposing no action is taken when public Facebook pages do this, then what is there to prevent the media itself from publishing such articles in the future?

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: If we accept such faking as normal, then you can see that the line between that and the current position of the UK almost disappears.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: You will then get in the mainstream media the headlines I earlier spoke about – about judges, abusing them and other similar sorts of things.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We should not get there and it will be a sad day for Singapore if we do get there.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Why did the Government not amend the law earlier?

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I said earlier that since 1976, the position has been settled, clear law from the time the Tay Choo Wah	case was decided.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: There must be many others which are unreported.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: So, the position has been consistently applied by the Courts over 40 years.

sections.label: Lacuna in section 409
sections.summary: Section 409 does not apply to directors and senior officers as construed by the Court of Appeal, and this lacuna should be fixed.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The law, as drafted, is wide enough to deal with people who act with criminal intention, conduct, misuse property.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: There is a lacuna in that section 409 does not apply to directors, senior officers in the way the Court of Appeal has construed it, and we should fix that lacuna.

sections.label: Cases involving directors before Courts
sections.summary: For cases involving directors or senior officers already before the Courts, the law as determined by the Court of Appeal must now be applied.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: For the cases involving directors, or similar sorts of senior officers, where the cases are already before the Courts, obviously, you will now have to apply the law as determined by the Court of Appeal.

sections.label: Section 409 drafted some time ago
sections.summary: They feel that section 409 was drafted some time ago.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: In summary, they feel that when the law was drafted, when section 409 was drafted, it was some time ago.
